Both attaching maps are null because the truncated simplex skeletons P_A,P_B are path-connected when m,n>=q+2. Contractible attachments split as suspensions, and uniform-matroid skeletons have the stated explicit pivot-matching sphere wedges, proving every integral homotopy claim. The standalone direct-geodesic exhaustive verifier independently checks all faces and mod-two boundaries for seven triples and 6149 nonempty faces; finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite or integral proof.

value.rationale: Fault-tolerant visibility quantifies redundancy in network geodesic communication, and all feasible vertex placements form a natural hereditary simplicial complex. The finding gives complete three-parameter integral sphere-wedge homotopy with potentially mixed dimensions, full face counts and relative information across positive fault-tolerance levels, rather than a textbook extremal bound or a known q=1 polynomial. The split uses a nontrivial two-stage null-attachment argument, is robust across unbounded parameters, and provides concrete test families for topological visibility invariants.
